summary: Masaharu Anesaki (1873–1949) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo and Kiel University, and under Max Müller, Deussen, and Oldenberg. He held positions at the University of Tokyo, including library director (1923–1934).

Masaharu Imai (b. 1942) works in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He earned his doctorate at Tokyo University of Education in 1977, taught at Ibaraki University, and became professor emeritus at the University of Tsukuba in 2006.

Masahide Mori (b. 1962) specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Nagoya University and SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski, later serving as an assistant professor (around 1998–2007) and professor (around 2007) at Kanazawa University.
Masahiro Asada (b. 1945) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University, where he also served as an assistant professor from around 1983 to 1990.

Masahiro Inami (b. 1960) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework at Hiroshima University and held teaching appointments at Tokyo Gakugei University around 1991 and 2007.

Masahiro Kusunoki (1921–2009) was a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University from around 1950 to 1953 and later served there as professor and chair of religion and history of religion (around 1970–1985).

Masahiro Shimoda (b. 1957) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and computational fields. He completed multiple degrees at the University of Tokyo and also studied at the University of Delhi, later serving as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1994–2023).
Masahiro Takano (b. 1960) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he was also attested as a librarian in 1995.

Masakatsu Fujita (b. 1949) specializes in philosophy and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1968 to 1972 and served as head of its Department of the History of Japanese Philosophy from around 2001 to 2014.

Masakazu Tanaka (b. 1955) works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Tohoku University and earned his Ph.D. from the London School of Economics, University of London, later serving as an assistant professor at Kyoto University (1988–2019).

Masako Keta (b. 1953) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at Kyoto University under Yoshinori Takeuchi. She held posts at Kanazawa University before serving as professor of philosophy of religion at Kyoto University (2000–2018).

Masamichi Asukai (1934–2000) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University from around 1952 to 1956 and later held an academic post there from around 1969 to 1998.

Masamichi Ichigo (b. 1941) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University and Kyoto University under Susumu Yamaguchi, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Gadjin Nagao, later serving as professor at Kyoto Sangyo University and president of Kyoto Koka Women's University (2007).
Masamichi Sakai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Helmut Krasser in 2006.
Masanori Nakagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 1991) and as an assistant professor in the Faculty of Letters (attested 2002) at Chikushi Jogakuen University.
Masanori Shono works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts as an assistant professor at Osaka University (attested 2012) and as a researcher at the University of Munich (attested 2015).

Masao Abe (1915–2006) was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Tanabe, Hisamatsu, and Nishitani, and at Columbia under Niebuhr and Tillich, holding professorships at Kyoto University and Nara University.

Masao Sekine (1912–2000) was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1934 to 1938 and held an academic post at Tokyo University of Education from around 1953 to 1976.
Masao Shizutani (b. 1925) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held assistant professorships at Josai University and at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested 1974).
Masaru Akimoto is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who served as a faculty professor in the Department of Contemporary Society at Kyoto Women's University (attested 2002 and 2015).
